Title: Ampang Jaya police probe viral TikTok assault and multi-car collision
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — Police are investigating a case of vandalism and voluntarily causing hurt after a car collided with several parked vehicles and a related assault, which went viral on TikTok.
Ampang Jaya district police chief ACP Khairul Anuar Khalid said in a statement today that the incident happened on September 26 at about 7am, when the complainant picked up a female friend, identified only as Nadia, from her home to go hiking at Bukit Melati, Nilai.
After the hike, the complainant drove Nadia home to Pangsapuri Sri Intan. There, the complainant was approached by three men, one of whom knocked on the driver's-side window and told the complainant to get out.
The complainant, who did not know the men, became frightened and accelerated forward, hitting several cars parked at the location.
The statement said one of the men then stood on the car's bonnet and was struck by three unidentified men in front of Orkid Apartment. The incident was later shared widely on TikTok.
Police are investigating under Section 427 of the Penal Code for mischief causing loss or damage, which carries a jail term of up to five years, a fine, or both. They are also investigating under Section 323 for voluntarily causing hurt, which carries up to one year in jail, a fine of up to RM2,000, or both.
Khairul Anuar urged members of the public with information on the case to come forward to assist investigators. He also advised the public not to speculate about the incident.

Title: Malaysia, UNODC strengthen cooperation to tackle complex transnational crimes, says Saifuddin Nasution
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — Malaysia aims to strengthen cooperation with the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) through more practical and result-oriented initiatives to address the increasingly complex threat of transnational organised crime.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the matter was discussed during his meeting with the UNODC regional representative for South-east Asia and the Pacific on the final day of his working visit to Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates (UAE), in conjunction with the 15th United Nations Congress on Crime Prevention and Criminal Justice.
He said during the meeting, both sides exchanged views on the increasingly complex landscape of transnational organised crime, particularly criminal networks exploiting digital technology to expand their activities across borders and jurisdictions.
“As a country strategically located in the heart of Asean, Malaysia takes these developments seriously. Our approach involves not only integrated enforcement but also prevention, cutting off illicit financial flows and strengthening regional and international cooperation,” he said in a statement posted on his social media page yesterday.
Elaborating, Saifuddin Nasution said the discussions also focused on efforts to tackle cyber-enabled organised crime, the illicit trafficking of people and contraband, as well as the misuse of emerging technologies by criminal networks.
He said Malaysia recognised the importance of UNODC continuing to support Asean countries through regional capacity building, information sharing and exchange of best practices.
“Cross-border threats continue to evolve and expand, and strong cooperation networks with regional and international partners are an important part of our efforts to ensure Malaysia’s security remains safeguarded,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Mohamad Hasan urges stronger Asean connectivity, eyes freer region with EU‑style movement
Article:
NEW YORK, Sept 28 — Asean needs to continue strengthening connectivity among its member states as a step towards creating a more open and integrated region, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan.
He said Malaysia aspired to see Asean develop into a freer region over the next 10 to 12 years, including exploring the free movement of people, similar to that practised in the European Union (EU).
“Connectivity among Asean countries needs to be effective,” he said during a question-and-answer session at a gathering with the Malaysian diaspora here on Saturday.
Mohamad said although the aspiration could not be fully realised under current circumstances due to differences in policies and laws among member states, this should not prevent Asean from achieving the vision.
He added that the effort should be viewed as a long-term process requiring preparation and gradual change.
Meanwhile, he said Malaysia needs to prepare its people, particularly by strengthening the education system for the younger generation, to face broader competition in a more open Asean.
“Are we ready, or have we prepared our Malaysian children to compete with children from Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines and other Asean countries?” he said.
Earlier, during a joint press conference with Malaysian media, Mohamad said Asean should continue playing the role of a middle power amid global geopolitical and economic uncertainty.
He said the international community is increasingly looking towards Asean to make its voice heard because of its position as a strong bloc, its ability to articulate a more effective common position on global issues and its significant economic potential. — Bernama

Title: Ministry reviews university holdings, UiTM team formed to safeguard Bumiputera institution’s future
Article:
ASTANA (Kazakhstan), Sept 28 —The Ministry of Higher Education (MOHE) began reviewing and restructuring public university holding companies last year, including UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd, said its Minister, Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir.
He said the move was taken to ensure university holding companies could function more effectively and contribute to their respective institutions, particularly after the government stopped fully funding universities’ financial needs in 2017.
“We have asked for all university holdings to be reviewed. Since last year, I have asked that we look at how to restructure the existing holding companies at universities.
“What we found was that some holdings were not functioning very well. That was the first step we took, and we have already begun several rounds of reviews to reassess these holdings, including UiTM Holdings,” he said.
He said this to Bernama here yesterday during the official visit to Kazakhstan for the Malaysia-Central Asia Higher Education Forum 2026 (MAHEF2026), when asked about MOHE’s follow-up action after Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim yesterday called for a review of UiTM Holdings’ management and governance following losses incurred by the company.
Zambry said some university holding companies had recorded profits while others had incurred losses, as such the business models of better-performing companies could serve as examples for others.
On UiTM, he said that a team had been established to comprehensively review efforts to strengthen the university, including aspects related to its holding company.
He said the team included Dr Nungsari Ahmad Radhi, Datuk Dr Hamzah Kassim, UiTM Board of Directors chairman Tan Sri Mohd Khamil Jamil and former Minister of Higher Education Tan Sri Idris Jusoh.
“We have set up a new team to look comprehensively at how we can reassess UiTM, and this also involves its holdings and so on.
“UiTM is a very important Bumiputera higher education institution that we need to safeguard and uphold to ensure that that no negative elements take root within it,” he said.
Zambry said he measures announced by the Prime Minister yesterday aligned with efforts already undertaken by MOHE, and the ministry would continue with the review.
UiTM Holdings was previously reported to have recorded cumulative pre-tax losses of approximately RM157 million for the 2017, 2018, 2019 and 2021 financial years. — Bernama

Title: Malaysian Embassy distributes dry food to staff and citizens hit by Bangkok floods
Article:
BANGKOK, Sept 28 — The Malaysian Embassy in Bangkok distributed dry food supplies to 10 Malaysians and locally recruited embassy staff who were directly affected by the floods in the Thai capital.
Malaysian Ambassador to Thailand Datuk Wan Zaidi Wan Abdullah said the dry food supplies, which could be stored for an extended period, were distributed to those affected on Sunday.
“The aid was handed to 10 recipients identified as being directly affected by the floods, comprising locally recruited embassy staff and Malaysians in the surrounding areas,” he told Bernama.
He added that the assistance was an early emergency intervention aimed at easing the burden of those facing disruptions to food supplies and daily necessities due to the floods.
He said the initiative also reflected the Malaysian Embassy’s concern for the welfare of affected Malaysians and its staff.
The aid distribution mission was led by Wan Zaidi as head of mission, while the on-ground distribution and coordination were headed by Malaysian Defence Attaché to Thailand Brig Gen Datuk Samsul Rizal Musa.
The aid distribution exercise was carried out from 10am to 7pm on Sunday.
Meanwhile, Wan Zaidi said the embassy would continue to monitor the flood situation in Bangkok and provide assistance to affected Malaysians and embassy staff.
He also advised Malaysians in affected areas to remain vigilant amid forecasts of continued rain until Sept 30 and to refer to the official travel advisory issued by the embassy from time to time. — Bernama

Title: From Mat Kilau to flying Malays: How communal anxieties fuel alternative history publishers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — From claiming that ancient Malays could fly to asserting that they taught the Romans naval shipbuilding, former linguistics professor Solehah Yaacob has drawn international ridicule while stirring passionate debate at home.
Although she was dismissed by the International Islamic University Malaysia in April, her revisionist claims retain a fervent following.
Boasting over 500,000 followers across Facebook and TikTok, Solehah continues to draw thousands of viewers, while her in-person Lost Malay History and Civilisation seminars remain in high demand,
The Straits Times
reported.
Sociologists trace the phenomenon to contemporary communal insecurities.
Aziff Azuddin of Iman Research said: “My reading is that the multicultural landscape of Malaysia, as well as Malay socio-political and economic anxieties, is why nativists, right-wingers – and people like Solehah – have such a purchase among some sections of the Malay community.”
Despite comprising over 60 per cent of Malaysia's 34 million citizens and holding constitutionally protected status, persistent economic anxieties continue to feed fears of marginalisation among some in the community, creating fertile ground for historical revisionism.
The revisionist push extends beyond social media personalities. Academics such as Universiti Sains Malaysia historian Azmi Arifin have questioned standard history syllabuses for over-relying on British colonial perspectives, arguing that terms like “feudal” fail to capture traditional Malay governance. He noted that anti-colonial figures like Pahang warrior Mat Kilau were unfairly branded as “rebels”.
Denying the pre-Islamic past
To assert historical supremacy, fringe revisionists often attempt to erase Malaysia's pre-Islamic heritage.
In a lecture in September, Solehah dismissed the country’s archaeological Hindu-Buddhist past as “mere propaganda” concocted by Western colonisers. Her videos blend local folklore with religious scripture, claiming that the prophet Abraham was Malay and that Moses visited Kedah's Gunung Jerai.
Cultural historian Eddin Khoo argued that defining Malay identity exclusively through a puritanical religious lens has made the region's pre-Islamic heritage uncomfortable for nativists.
“Solehah is a fantasist, but people want to believe that about themselves,” Khoo said. “To them, everything must trace back to their puritanical idea of Islam; otherwise, it is illegitimate.”
Khoo noted the irony in seeking monocultural purity when historical Malay societies were deeply cosmopolitan, pointing to Portuguese chronicler Tomé Pires’s account of 84 languages spoken in 16th-century Melaka.
Commercial appetite for alternative history
The demand for revisionist narratives is also commercial. Novelist and sociologist Faizal Musa pointed to the popularity of alternative history publishers such as The Patriots, whose online bookstore commands over 52,000 followers.
“Simple explanations are often seen as more appealing and credible than complex ones, particularly when they appear capable of being tested or disproved,” Faizal said, adding that such revisionist trends are a global phenomenon.
Khoo cautioned that unchecked pseudohistory erodes public historical literacy: “Myth has an important role in not just Malay, but also Asian history; however, this is not even myth – it is fantasy.”

Title: Johor air quality clears up, Serian lingers as Malaysia’s lone haze hotspot
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — Serian in Sarawak was the only location in Malaysia recording an unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) reading as of 8.30am today, according to the Department of Environment (DoE).
DoE surveillance data showed the monitoring station at IPD Serian logging an API reading of 152, placing it within the unhealthy threshold of 101 to 200. No other monitoring point in the country registered elevated pollution levels this morning.
The reading marks a slight deterioration from the 141 recorded in Serian at 4pm yesterday, when it was similarly the sole affected district in Sarawak.
In contrast, air quality across southern Peninsular Malaysia showed marked overnight improvement. Four industrial and urban hotspots in Johor that recorded unhealthy readings yesterday afternoon, namely Pasir Gudang (161), Kota Tinggi (159), Pengerang (158), and Larkin (152), all dropped off the department's unhealthy register by this morning.
As of late yesterday afternoon, 51 monitoring stations nationwide, including the federal capital Kuala Lumpur, recorded moderate air quality, while 12 stations logged good air quality levels.
Under standard DoE metrics, API readings between 0 and 50 are classified as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and 301 and above as hazardous.

Title: Police confirm excavator operator drowned after machine overturned during Tasik Bera cleaning work
Article:
KUANTAN, Sept 28 — An excavator operator was found drowned after the machine he was operating overturned during cleaning work at Tasik Bera, Bera yesterday.
Bera district police chief Supt Zulkiflee Nazir said his team received a report regarding the incident at around 2.10pm Sunday.
He said the deceased was Alief Daniel Haqim Abdullah, 26, while another worker who survived was Muhammad Aiman Fikri Mohd Azhar, 28.
“Based on the information received, there were two workers at the time of the incident. One managed to escape while the other was trapped in the machine,” he said in a statement yesterday.
In addition, Pahang Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department assistant director (Operations) Mohd Salahuddin Isa said in a statement that the victim’s body was found trapped in the cabin of the excavator before being extricated at 4.10pm.
“The victim was unconscious when brought ashore before being pronounced dead by the health personnel who arrived at the scene,” he also said.
Zulkiflee added that the victim’s body was sent to the hospital for an autopsy. — Bernama

Title: Boom gates, guardhouses and access cards: Here are 23 rules guarded Klang Valley neighbourhoods must follow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — Guardhouses, boom gates and security guards have become a familiar sight in residential neighbourhoods across the Klang Valley, but putting them in place is not simply a matter of getting enough neighbours to agree and hiring a security company.
There are rules governing how guarded communities are established, where a guardhouse can be built, when a boom gate can be closed, whether residents can be forced to participate and even where speed bumps can be placed.
And the rules are not exactly the same across Kuala Lumpur and Selangor.
In Kuala Lumpur, City Hall (DBKL) uses the PLANMalaysia guideline as a reference for guarded neighbourhoods.
The four Selangor local authorities
Malay Mail
is focusing on — Ampang Jaya Municipal Council (MPAJ), Subang Jaya City Council (MBSJ), Shah Alam City Council (MBSA) and Petaling Jaya City Council (MBPJ) — generally follow the Selangor Housing and Property Board (LPHS) framework, with individual councils setting additional requirements according to local conditions.
PLANMalaysia’s 2019 guideline was introduced to guide state and local authorities, technical agencies and residents’ associations in establishing and managing guarded communities in non-strata housing. It replaced the 2010 guideline.
The guideline itself notes that its implementation must be read together with existing laws and other relevant guidelines, and that local authorities can impose conditions according to their respective jurisdictions.
Here is what residents need to know.
1. First, how many residents have to agree?
This is one of the biggest differences.
Under the PLANMalaysia guideline, at least 85 per cent of residents must agree before an application can be made.
The percentage is calculated based on occupied homes. Residents are defined as homeowners or tenants living in the proposed guarded community, while homes that are not continuously occupied are excluded.
In Selangor, the LPHS framework provides for:
75 per cent consent for a guarded community using a manual boom gate; and
100 per cent consent for an automatic boom gate or access-card system.
The Selangor government has confirmed that the LPHS guideline remains the applicable framework, with individual local authorities able to impose more detailed requirements according to their respective areas and circumstances.
For DBKL, the current publicly cited requirement is at least 81 per cent consent for a guarded neighbourhood scheme, while automatic boom gates using facial recognition require 100 per cent consent.
So a neighbourhood does not necessarily need unanimous support simply to establish a guarded community.
But it is a different story if residents want an automatic access system.
Boom gates controlling vehicle access at a guarded residential area. Guidelines differ depending on whether access is manual or automated. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
2. Getting the required percentage does not mean residents can be forced to join
This is an important protection for residents who disagree.
The PLANMalaysia guideline says the process of obtaining consent must not involve coercion or pressure on residents who do not agree.
The Selangor framework likewise states that there should be no coercion to join the scheme.
So if a neighbourhood reaches the required threshold, that does not mean every resident has automatically agreed to participate.
3. A resident who does not join cannot be locked out
This is perhaps the most important practical rule.
The PLANMalaysia guideline states that residents who do not participate in the scheme cannot be prevented from entering their homes at any time.
That means a resident who refuses to join cannot be denied access to his or her home merely for not participating in the scheme.
The Selangor guidelines contain the same basic principle.
4. A boom gate cannot simply be used to block access
The guidelines also prohibit vehicles from being obstructed when entering or leaving the neighbourhood.
This is significant because a guarded community does not automatically turn a public residential road into a private one.
PLANMalaysia’s guideline requires the scheme to have access arrangements that do not obstruct traffic, while its management conditions state that public authorities and members of the public must be allowed to enter and use public roads and facilities.
The Selangor guidelines similarly prohibit guards from denying lawful access to residents, members of the public and authorities.
This does not prevent an approved guarded scheme from operating security procedures at its entrance, but those arrangements cannot be used to bar people who are entitled to enter.
5. The boom gate is generally supposed to operate only from midnight to 6am
Under the PLANMalaysia guideline, a boom gate is generally allowed to operate from midnight to 6am.
A local authority may consider allowing it to remain closed 24 hours a day, but only if security guards are stationed there around the clock and can open the barrier whenever necessary.
This means a neighbourhood cannot simply install a boom gate and keep it permanently closed because residents prefer tighter access control.
6. Automatic access systems are a different matter
The PLANMalaysia guideline says automatic access cards can only be allowed if 100 per cent of residents agree.
Selangor’s LPHS framework similarly sets 100 per cent consent for automatic boom gates or access-card systems.
The Selangor government has said the higher threshold is intended to protect residents’ rights and avoid disputes over access between participating and non-participating households.
This contrasts with manual boom gates, for which the Selangor framework sets a 75 per cent consent threshold.
7. An automatic system does not necessarily mean one lane for everyone
This is where individual council rules become more detailed.
MBPJ’s guidelines allow an access-card arrangement to be considered with two separate lanes — one for residents and another for visitors — provided there are 24-hour guards and the other MBPJ conditions are met.
MPAJ also has requirements governing arrangements for residents and visitors when considering automated access systems.
So while the basic PLANMalaysia guideline does not prescribe a universal “resident lane” and “visitor lane” for every guarded community, individual councils may set more detailed conditions when automatic access is proposed.
A security guard attends to a motorist at the entrance to a guarded residential neighbourhood. Guarded-community schemes remain subject to local authority rules on access and security procedures. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
8. There are even rules on where speed bumps can go
This is another detail many residents may not know.
PLANMalaysia allows speed breakers or road humps to be installed before and after the guardhouse.
But the guideline does not give residents a free hand to put them wherever they want. They must comply with specifications issued by the relevant local authority.
MBSA, for example, gives specific dimensions based on road width.
Its guideline states that for a 50ft road, the road hump should be 5ft wide, while for a 66ft road, it should be 10ft wide.
So even something as seemingly simple as a speed bump outside a guardhouse is subject to council requirements.
9. The guardhouse itself cannot just be built anywhere
PLANMalaysia says the guardhouse should be located on the road shoulder and must not obstruct traffic.
It cannot be built on or in the middle of the road under the national guideline.
The guideline also says the guardhouse cannot be built until the relevant temporary construction permit or approval has been obtained.
The national guideline specifies a maximum size of 1.8m by 2.4m, although Selangor councils have their own specifications.
For example, MPAJ, MBSJ and MBPJ generally use a 6ft by 8ft specification, while MBSA has different dimensions depending on whether a toilet is included.
10. A permanent guardhouse needs another layer of approval
If a guardhouse occupies the road shoulder and is a permanent structure, the residents’ association may need a Temporary Occupation Licence (TOL) from the District and Land Office under Section 65 of the National Land Code 1965.
The PLANMalaysia guideline also requires the guardhouse location to be shown on plans submitted to the relevant land office and local authority.
So a residents’ association cannot simply construct a permanent guardhouse on the road reserve because residents have voted for it.
11. There should be at least two access routes for emergencies
PLANMalaysia’s technical requirements say a guarded community should have at least two entry and exit routes for emergency purposes.
This is separate from the question of whether there is a residents’ lane and a visitors’ lane.
The requirement is about ensuring sufficient access in an emergency, rather than simply creating a convenient arrangement for residents and visitors.
12. Entrance gateways may require separate approval
The PLANMalaysia guideline restricts structures that span or obstruct the entrance road as part of a guarded-neighbourhood scheme.
However, individual councils may have their own procedures for considering entrance gateways.
MBPJ, for example, allows applications for entrance gateways to be considered separately through the planning-permission process, subject to the necessary technical approvals.
So residents should not assume that approval for a guarded-community scheme automatically allows them to build a large gateway or arch over the entrance road.
13. You cannot simply build a wall around the neighbourhood
Perimeter fencing is generally prohibited.
PLANMalaysia says perimeter fencing that surrounds the guarded community and blocks access is not allowed.
However, a local authority can consider fencing where there are legitimate safety concerns, such as a large drain, river or highway.
The Selangor councils have adopted broadly similar provisions.
A guardhouse and access barriers at a guarded neighbourhood in Sungai Buloh. Residents’ associations must comply with local authority requirements when operating such schemes. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
14. Guards cannot demand your identity card
Security guards are not allowed to keep or demand a member of the public’s or a resident’s identity card simply as a condition of entering the neighbourhood.
The PLANMalaysia guideline says it is sufficient for guards to record a visitor’s name and vehicle registration number.
MBSA goes further by prohibiting guards from scanning identity cards.
15. Government officers and emergency services cannot simply be turned away
The guideline requires security guards to allow members of the public and authorities to enter the housing area and use public roads and facilities.
This means a guardhouse is not a checkpoint with the authority to decide that government officers, enforcement personnel or other authorised parties cannot enter.
MBPJ’s guidelines also specifically require residents’ associations to brief guards on the identities of agencies such as MBPJ, the police, the Fire and Rescue Department, the Land Office and ambulance services.
16. The neighbourhood generally has to be a cul-de-sac
PLANMalaysia says guarded communities should only be established in residential areas that do not have roads connecting them to neighbouring communities.
In other words, the model is intended for areas where roads effectively terminate within the neighbourhood rather than forming an important through-route.
The guideline describes this as allowing only cul-de-sac-type areas, subject to the local authority’s discretion.
17. Public facilities can disqualify an area
A guarded community is generally not supposed to be established in an area containing public facilities such as schools, mosques, public halls and public open spaces, or areas served by public bus routes.
The principle is that a security arrangement for one residential community should not prevent wider public access to shared facilities.
The Selangor councils have adapted this differently.
For example, MBSA allows certain smaller shared facilities such as small surau and Rukun Tetangga posts, while excluding larger facilities such as schools, halls and football fields.
18. The security company must be properly registered
The residents’ association cannot simply hire anyone to stand at the guardhouse.
PLANMalaysia requires the appointed security company to be registered with the Home Ministry (KDN), with the employment and operation of guards subject to the relevant requirements.
The guideline also states that the appointment of security guards must comply with the Private Agencies Act 1971 and KDN requirements.
A residential entrance with controlled access. Rules governing guarded communities cover issues including barriers, access arrangements, guardhouses and residents’ rights. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
19. Guards cannot use dogs for patrols
This may come as a surprise to some residents.
The PLANMalaysia guideline specifically says security guards are not allowed to use dogs for patrol and security purposes.
20. A guarded community is not supposed to be permanent by default
PLANMalaysia says guarded communities are not encouraged as a long-term arrangement.
The national guideline also provides for a permit system rather than treating the scheme as a permanent change to the neighbourhood.
Under PLANMalaysia’s application procedure, the permit is valid for one year and runs alongside the expiry of the Temporary Occupation Licence for the guardhouse.
The Selangor councils have their own approval periods, generally allowing temporary schemes for a limited period and requiring renewal.
21. The residents’ association has to put up a notice before applying
It is not simply an internal residents’ association decision.
PLANMalaysia requires the applicant to put up a banner informing residents at the main entrance for 30 days after submitting the application.
The application itself also has to go through the local authority’s One Stop Centre (OSC).
22. The approval permit has to be displayed
Once approved, the residents’ association has to display the valid permit at the guardhouse or on the notice board at the main entrance so it can be inspected by the authorities.
Operating a guarded community without the necessary permit, or constructing a guardhouse without approval, can result in enforcement action.
23. What happens if the scheme is cancelled?
The neighbourhood is supposed to be returned to its original condition.
PLANMalaysia says that when guarded-community status is removed, the residents’ association must notify the local authority and remove the guardhouse, boom gate and fencing, where applicable.

Title: Family spokesman: Malaysia sought wider Nepal search for 55 uncontactable citizens, but access was limited
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 27 — Malaysia initially requested that the search and rescue (SAR) operation involving 55 Malaysians who are still uncontactable in Nepal cover the area from Rasuwagadhi to Syabrubesi, but the national team was only allowed to conduct searches in certain areas.
Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (MASFIH) spokesman Dr Manivannan Rethinam said the matter was conveyed to the next of kin during a closed-door meeting with government agencies at Wisma Putra today.
He said the families raised the question of why the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) operation was not focused on Rasuwagadhi, which is a border area between Nepal and Tibet, believed to be one of the last locations many Malaysians were involved.
According to him, the Chargé d’Affaires ad interim of the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu, Mohd Firdaus Azman, explained that Malaysia had requested the Nepalese authorities to extend the search area from Rasuwagadhi to Syabrubesi. However, the permission granted by the Nepalese authorities to the Malaysian team only covers certain areas, including Timure.
“Their (SMART) search area is focused on areas C and D. They cover from Timure to Syabrubesi. That is not the focal area where many Malaysians are missing because we have information on the last known locations and most of them are concentrated in the Rasuwagadhi area, on the Tibet-Nepal border,” he told the media after a nearly four-hour briefing session here today.
Manivannan said the families understand that the SMART operation area is subject to the approval of the Nepalese authorities and that the matter is beyond the team’s control.
He simultaneously expressed appreciation for SMART’s efforts, which also provided explanations to the families about the operations and challenges faced by the team during their time in Nepal.
According to Manivannan, the families also inquired about the possibility of the victims still being found alive.
He said that the SMART commander Senior Fire and Rescue Officer 1 (PgKB 1) Abdul Manaf Che Isa had said that the possibility still exists if there are victims in remote areas or villages in the mountainous region, but the chances are very slim.
“As family members, we still hope for the best. But we also have to move on to the next stage,” he said.
Previously, the SMART Team, consisting of 11 members, was sent to Nepal on September 5 and conducted ground searches and monitoring using drones in areas approved and deemed safe by the Nepalese authorities before returning to Malaysia on September 14.
In addition, Manivannan said the families were informed that Nepal would process the DNA samples from the disaster victims’ bodies to match them with the family’s DNA profiles.
He said the families had previously been informed about the report that Nepal needed assistance to carry out the DNA process due to a lack of expertise.
However, based on today’s briefing, the Nepalese authorities now have sufficient expertise and will carry out the process themselves.
“So far, they are only collecting DNA but it has not been processed yet. Previously, there were media reports in Nepal stating that Nepal needed assistance to process DNA because they lacked expertise. But today, Firdaus from the Malaysian Embassy in Nepal said that Nepal already has enough expertise. They will process it themselves,” he said.
Manivannan said that essentially, the DNA profile obtained from the families will be used for matching with the DNA from the found remains.
According to him, if there is a match, it can help the authorities identify the identity of the body in question.
Commenting on the procedure in the event of a DNA match, Manivannan said based on the explanation received by the families, DNA will be taken from the body before burial.
If a match with family members is later obtained, he said there is a process to retrieve the body to allow the family to conduct a ceremony or bring it home.
However, he emphasised that the families have not yet received official information regarding the entire procedure. — Bernama

Title: Man dies of rabies in Kedah’s first human case in 28 years
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Sept 27 — The State Health Department (JKN) of Kedah has reported the state’s first human rabies case since 1998, involving a 31-year-old man from Kubang Pasu who died today after being bitten by a stray dog in August.
It said that the victim sought treatment at a healthcare facility after the incident but did not receive rabies post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP).
“On September 18, the victim began experiencing fatigue, weakness and numbness in the right upper limb. The symptoms progressed to difficulty swallowing, hydrophobia, aerophobia, anxiety and behavioural changes on September 22, consistent with the clinical manifestations of rabies.
“The following day, the victim sought treatment again and was referred for further treatment before being admitted to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU),” it said in a statement today.
It said clinical samples taken on Sept 24 were confirmed by laboratory tests two days later to be positive for rabies.
“Following the confirmation, Kedah JKN, the Kubang Pasu District Health Office, the Kedah Veterinary Services Department and relevant agencies implemented control and prevention measures, including active case detection, health education, enhanced surveillance of animal-bite cases, risk assessment and control of stray animals in the affected area.
“As this is the first human rabies case reported in Kedah since 1998, the Ministry of Health (MOH), together with Kedah JKN and relevant agencies, is conducting a comprehensive epidemiological investigation to identify the source of infection and route of exposure,” it added.
The investigation includes examining the victim’s travel and exposure history, identifying contacts and risk factors, and analysing the timeline of events to determine the source and factors associated with the infection.
Kedah JKN said control measures were also being strengthened under the ‘One Health’ approach, involving human exposure management, surveillance of animal-bite cases and monitoring and risk assessment of dogs and other potentially exposed animals in high-risk areas.
It said that as of August 2026, a total of 502 animal bite and scratch cases had been reported in Kedah, with 65.3 per cent involving dogs, 23.1 per cent cats and 11.6 per cent other animals, adding that of these, 56.2 per cent involved domestic animals and 43.8 per cent stray animals.
It reminded the public that rabies can be transmitted through bites, scratches or exposure to the saliva of infected animals, and urged pet owners to ensure their dogs and cats receive anti-rabies vaccinations.
Kedah JKN also said that anyone bitten or scratched by an animal should immediately wash the wound with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek medical attention at a public or private healthcare facility for risk assessment and appropriate treatment. — Bernama

Title: All Malaysian Indian Progressive Front seeks BN membership — and a shot at contesting Penang seats
Article:
BUTTERWORTH, Sept 27 — The All Malaysian Indian Progressive Front (IPF) has applied to become a component party of Barisan Nasional (BN), with Penang as the starting point before the move is taken to the national level.
Its president Datuk T. Loganathan said the application was driven by its longstanding loyalty to BN, despite never having been given any positions.
He said IPF had remained loyal to BN even after the coalition lost the 14th general election (GE14) in 2018, when several other component parties chose to leave.
“IPF hopes its application to become a BN component party will receive due consideration, with Penang serving as the starting point before the initiative is taken to the national level,” he said in his speech at the Penang IPF assembly here today.
He also hoped that the BN leadership would consider giving IPF the opportunity to contest suitable state seats where the party had a potential to win.
Meanwhile, Penang BN chairman Datuk Musa Sheikh Fadzir said he would bring the application to the Umno supreme council meeting before it was submitted to the Umno president, who is also the BN chairman.
Musa said Penang IPF was among the organisations that had actively supported BN, including during by-elections and state elections. — Bernama

Title: Wisma Putra: Nepal weighs legal measures for those still unaccounted for after Aug 26 floods, including 55 Malaysians
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 27 — The Nepalese government is considering legal measures to address cases involving individuals whose status remains undetermined, including foreign nationals, following floods and landslides in the country.
In a statement Sunday, Malaysia’s Foreign Ministry said the proposed measures are still subject to Nepal’s domestic legal processes and have yet to take effect.
“The Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu will continue to liaise with the Nepalese authorities to obtain clarification on the relevant processes and documentation should the measures be implemented.
“The Malaysian government will also continue to engage with the Nepalese authorities and coordinate with Malaysian agencies on the relevant processes,” it said.
Wisma Putra said any determination of an individual’s status and issuance of official documentation would be subject to the relevant laws and procedures and the respective authorities in Nepal and Malaysia.
On Sunday, Wisma Putra met 95 next-of-kin and family representatives representing the families of 55 Malaysians who remain uncontactable following the floods and landslides in Nepal on August 26.
The session was held to brief families on the latest verified developments and provide an opportunity for them to raise questions directly with the ministry and agencies involved in the efforts.
The briefing involved the Malaysian Special Search and Rescue Team (SMART), Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), Department of Chemistry Malaysia, Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu, Malaysian Embassy in Beijing and National Registration Department (JPN).
Each agency provided updates on matters under its respective jurisdiction during the closed-door meeting, which began at 10.15am and ended at about 3pm.
Wisma Putra said counsellors from the Social Welfare Department (JKM) were also present to provide support to family members throughout the session.
“As the efforts have now entered a long-term phase, the session also discussed legal and administrative processes that may apply to the families of affected Malaysians,” added the statement.
Wisma Putra also expressed appreciation to the National Security Council (MKN), National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), SMART, PDRM, Department of Chemistry Malaysia, Ministry of Health, Attorney General’s Chambers, JPN, JKM and all agencies involved for their cooperation and assistance throughout the operation, including support for the affected families.
“The Malaysian government also extends its appreciation to the Government of Nepal and relevant Nepalese authorities for their continued cooperation.”
The Foreign Ministry also urged the public and media to respect the privacy of the affected families and refrain from speculating about any individual whose status has yet to be confirmed.
The floods and debris flow on August 26, triggered by an ice and rock collapse in the upper catchment of the Lhende Khola in Tibet, reportedly killed more than 1,450 people, while thousands remain unaccounted for. — Bernama

Title: RM1b resort, 700 jobs: Papar’s first five-star hotel due in 2027
Article:
PAPAR, Sept 27 — Papar’s first five-star hotel, InterContinental Sabah Kota Kinabalu Resort in Melinsung, is expected to begin operations in December 2027.
Papar Member of Parliament Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the RM1 billion project, developed by Taiwan-based Sinyi Group, covers more than 80 acres (32.4 hectares), with IHG Hotels & Resorts as its operating partner.
Based on a briefing by the developer, he said overall construction progress stood at about 34.1 per cent as of September 2026, while the main hotel had reached 47.7 per cent completion.
“The main hotel is targeted to begin operations in December 2027, followed by the entire resort in 2028. Upon completion, the project is expected to create about 700 new jobs,” he told reporters after visiting the project site here today.
Armizan, who is also domestic trade and cost of living minister, said the project was planned to have 418 rooms and accommodation units and was expected to become an international-standard tourism destination in the district.
Armizan said efforts to attract the investment began in October 2021 when he joined several Sinyi Group directors and district officers to visit a number of potential sites for resort development.
“Sinyi Group finally chose Papar for its investment to develop an international-standard tourism destination, the InterContinental Sabah Kota Kinabalu Resort,” he said.
The project progress visit was also attended by Kawang assemblyman Datuk Seri Gulamhaidar Khan Bahadar and local leaders, who received a briefing from the developer before inspecting construction work at the site.
“My hope from the beginning has been for this investment to deliver benefits beyond the development of a resort. It should create jobs for local people and generate economic spillovers for food, transport, supply and tourism service operators in Papar,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Dr Zaliha denies attending Myanmar refugee settlement ceremony, says viral claim is false
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 27 — Former minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa denied allegations that she had attended, officiated, or been involved in any groundbreaking ceremonies for new settlements for Myanmar refugees.
She emphasised that the allegations circulating on social media are false and malicious, in addition to linking a photograph of her with an individual to something that never happened.
“I do not personally know the individual in question and do not have any relationship or dealings, whether official or unofficial, with him,” she said in a Facebook post today.
Dr Zaliha explained that based on the review, the circulated photo is believed to have been taken at the Asean Sustainable Urbanisation Forum (ASUF), Asean Governors and Mayors Forum (AGMF), and Meeting of Governors and Mayors of Asean Capitals (MGMAC) 2025 in the capital city on August 12, 2025.
According to her, she was invited to deliver a special address and subsequently attend the Joint Launch Ceremony for the programme, which was officiated by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof.
“The programme is open to the public to register as participants. Therefore, I certainly do not know the identity of every individual who attended.
“A photo with a participant does not mean I know the person, have a relationship with him, invited him personally, or support his views or actions,” she said.
The Sekijang Member of Parliament said she would report the matter to the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) regarding the dissemination of the post for review and appropriate action according to the law.
Meanwhile, Dr Zaliha said the allegation that she supported or facilitated the resettlement of new Myanmar refugees was also inconsistent with the record of actions she took while leading the Federal Territories Department.
She said that among the measures implemented was the establishment of the KL Strike Force as an integrated enforcement mechanism to address issues of security and public order, particularly in the capital, including the issue of the influx of foreign nationals and the illegal settlement of Myanmar refugees.
“In fact, the first operation of the KL Strike Force was to raid the illegal settlement of Myanmar refugees in Bandar Baru Sentul. Through KL Strike Force, I emphasised that action should be taken against illegal settlements and structures, unlicensed businesses, and foreign activities without proper authorisation,” she also said.
Therefore, she urged all parties not to take a single photo out of context to build a narrative that is not based on facts. — Bernama

Title: RM1m haul as GOF intercepts 15,000 coffee seedlings at Tanah Merah roadblock
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 27 — The General Operations Force (GOF) seized 15,000 robusta coffee seedlings and a lorry with a total value of RM1 million during a roadblock at Lalang Pepuyu, Tanah Merah, last night.
GOF Southeast Brigade commander SAC Ahmad Radzi Hussain said a 27-year-old man who was driving the lorry was detained during the operation at 11.30pm.
“An inspection of the lorry’s cargo compartment uncovered 15,000 robusta coffee seedlings believed to have been smuggled from Thailand.
“The total value of the seizure was estimated at RM1 million, comprising the lorry worth RM250,000 and the coffee seedlings worth RM750,000,” he said in a statement today.
He said preliminary investigation found that the man had collected the seedlings from an illegal jetty in the Lalang Pepuyu area to deliver them to a nursery in Johor for RM300 per delivery.
“All the seedlings were handed over to the Kota Bharu Agriculture Department for further action as they are suspected of containing pests,” he said.
Ahmad Radzi said the seedlings would be inspected before being disposed of, while a compound could be issued if the offence involving pests was confirmed.
The case is being investigated under the Plant Quarantine Act 1976 (Act 167), he added. — Bernama

Title: Anwar hails squash ace Ng Eain Yow after Asian Games gold secures LA28 Olympic berth
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 27 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim congratulated national squash ace Ng Eain Yow on defending his men’s singles gold medal at Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games today.
In a Facebook post, Anwar noted that Eain Yow had repeated the feat he achieved four years ago in Hangzhou, where he also won the gold medal.
“Four years ago in Hangzhou, the gold went to Eain Yow. Today, he has repeated that same success.
“A proud achievement that once again brings glory to Malaysia. Well done, Eain Yow!” he said.
Eain Yow retained the men’s singles gold medal after defeating India’s Abhay Singh 11-9, 11-5, 11-5 in the final at Nagoya Kinjofuto Arena today.
The victory also saw the Kuala Lumpur-born player secure an early ticket to Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games.
This gold medal marks Malaysia’s fifth at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Games, following two golds in karate and one each in e-sports and sepak takraw. — Bernama

Title: Two men found dead in separate Alor Gajah incidents, police rule out foul play
Article:
ALOR GAJAH, Sept 27 — Two men, aged 57 and 38, were found dead in separate incidents in Alor Gajah today.
Alor Gajah district police chief Supt Ahmad Abu Bakar said police received a report regarding the discovery of a 57-year-old man at 11.30am in an abandoned shophouse in Cherana Putih, Taboh Naning.
He said the body believed to have been dead for two days was discovered by a member of the public in the area.
“A preliminary examination of the body revealed no signs of foul play, and the victim is believed to have been in the area without his family’s knowledge,” he told reporters here today.
In a related development, Ahmad said the second case involved a 38-year-old man found dead in an apartment unit in Simpang Ampat at approximately noon.
He said the victim was a factory worker who lived alone, was discovered by his fiancée after failing to answer phone calls since the previous night.
The fiancée entered the home through a window and found the victim unconscious before calling an ambulance.
“No signs of break-in or foul play were detected in either incident, and the cases have been classified as sudden death (SDR).
“Both bodies have been taken to Alor Gajah Hospital for post-mortem to determine the exact cause of death,” he said. — Bernama

Title: JPJ seizes 3,790 luxury vehicles worth RM550m in nationwide crackdown since June 2025
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 27 — A total of 3,790 luxury vehicles worth an estimated RM550 million were seized by the Road Transport Department (JPJ) under Ops Luxury from June 2025 to yesterday for various offences.
JPJ senior director of enforcement Datuk Muhammad Kifli Ma Hassan said 785 vehicles were seized between June and December 2025, while another 3,005 were seized from January to September 26 this year.
He said Negeri Sembilan recorded the highest number of seizures with 469 vehicles, followed by Selangor (410), Kuala Lumpur (382), Johor (367) and Penang (357).
“Some luxury vehicle owners said they were reluctant to go to JPJ offices to renew their road tax because they had been blacklisted for previous offences.
“What is puzzling is that lower-income groups can come forward to renew their road tax, while owners of luxury vehicles from the T20 group give various reasons for not doing so, resulting in their vehicles being seized,” he told a press conference at the Panji JPJ Office here today.
He said investigations found that an estimated 20 per cent of the luxury vehicle owners were cosmetic entrepreneurs, influencers and businesspeople.
Muhammad Kifli said JPJ would continue Ops Luxury to ensure that all road users comply with the law, regardless of the price or type of vehicle or the status of its owner.
“Being able to afford a luxury vehicle comes with the responsibility to comply with the law. Owners and drivers are responsible for ensuring that all vehicle and driving documents remain valid, and that their vehicles meet all requirements before being driven on the road,” he said. — Bernama

Title: A month without answers: Families of missing Malaysians told Nepal search may soon end
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 27 — After more than a month of waiting without news, the families of Malaysians still missing following the flood disaster in Nepal are beginning to resign themselves to all possibilities when informed that the government of that country is considering ending the search and rescue (SAR) operations.
In a meeting with government agencies at Wisma Putra today, the next of kin were also briefed on the process related to the death certificates, which are being expedited to facilitate the families’ affairs.
S. Sankara, the son of a missing Malaysian, said Wisma Putra informed them that the Nepalese government is expected to conclude the rescue operation phase soon before transitioning to recovery operations.
“Based on the briefing received, the search and rescue operation is still ongoing at this time. The family was briefed on the documentation process, including the death certificate that will be issued by the Nepalese government,” he said to the media when met at the Wisma Putra compound here today.
The four-hour meeting, which started around 10.15 am and ended around 3 pm, involved briefings from several agencies regarding SAR operations, management of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) samples, as well as legal and documentation processes.
Meanwhile, Sankara said his family is trying to continue with their lives as best as they can despite still facing emotional pressure following the loss of his mother, K. Kalaimathi, 57, who was in Nepal for a religious ritual.
For Adura Masood, the wait for her husband, Dr. Mohd Padzil Daros, 63, is still not over.
“Not yet. No news,” she said when asked about any update on her husband.
Adura said today’s briefing explained the search efforts carried out by the involved teams, but there has not been much new development regarding the victim’s whereabouts.
“I don’t think there has been much (development). They explained what happened there, just a brief explanation. It’s just a briefing,” she said.
However, Adura believes that the team involved has done their best in the search effort.
“I think they have done their job,” she said.
Mohd Padzil was among the members of a group known as “Team Loe” who were reported missing when they were about 18 kilometres from the Rasuwagadhi-Kerung border.
The group was reported to be travelling from Kathmandu to the Nepal-Tibet border in a four-wheel-drive vehicle when the disaster struck the Rasuwa area.
Among those who participated in the journey were members of the special team from the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM), Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, and JBPM Fire and Rescue Operations Division deputy director Mohd Sani Harul.
Also participating in the same mission were Ganesh Neupane, Shabuddin Mun, Azman Karim, Muhammad Hazig Ismail, Mohd Nohan Salim, Jason Ngeow and Muhamad Nasir Abdul Talib.
Today’s meeting is the second following the government’s first official engagement with the affected families on Aug 30, five days after the incident on Aug 26, but not all families were represented at that time.
Among those involved are representatives from the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART), the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), the Malaysian Department of Chemistry, the National Registration Department (JPN), the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu, and the Department of Social Welfare (JKM).
The flood and debris flow on August 26, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche in the upper Lhende Khola watershed in Tibet, and reportedly claimed more than 1,450 lives, while thousands more remain unaccounted for. — Bernama

Title: Dr Wan Azizah wants women to make up at least 30pc of PKR candidates in Melaka
Article:
MELAKA, Sept 27 — The principle of justice must continue to be the cornerstone of PKR’s struggle as it faces the Melaka state election, said the party’s Advisory Council chairman Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail.
She said the party’s struggle was not merely about gaining power, but about ensuring that every Malaysian received the justice they deserved.
“We want every Malaysian to have justice. That is what we uphold in our party and in our struggle,” she told reporters after launching the Melaka Wanita PKR election machinery here today.
Also present were prime minister’s political secretary Datuk Azman Abidin and Melaka Wanita PKR chief Mahani Masban.
Dr Wan Azizah, who is also Bandar Tun Razak MP said PKR members must remain steadfast in upholding the principle despite various challenges, including the departure of some members from the party.
She said PKR’s long experience had shown that change did not come easily, but required sustained effort and commitment from party members.
Dr Wan Azizah urged Melaka Wanita PKR to play an important role in garnering voters’ support and strengthening the party’s spirit of struggle at the grassroots level.
She also expressed hope that Wanita PKR would be given the opportunity to contest in the state election, with women making up at least 30 per cent of the total candidates.
Meanwhile, Azman said PKR could spring a surprise in Melaka if it had a disciplined, well-trained and committed election machinery.
He said the party’s machinery needed to work harder, given that PKR currently held no seats in the Melaka State Legislative Assembly. — Bernama

Title: Calls unanswered, woman forces entry and finds fiancé dead in Melaka home
Article:
ALOR GAJAH, Sept 27 — A woman was left heartbroken after finding her fiancé lying lifeless in his home, having failed to reach him since last night.
The 38-year-old went to his house in Simpang Ampat around 11am today after growing anxious when her calls went unanswered,
Harian Metro
reported.
Alor Gajah district police chief Superintendent Ahmad Abu Bakar said she had gone to the man’s residence to look for him after being unable to contact him.
“On arriving, she entered the house through a window and found him inside the unit before calling for an ambulance. Further checks confirmed he had died,” he told the national daily.
The victim, who worked at a factory, is believed to have been living alone at the property.

Title: Amanah sets sights on 18 seats for GE16, but concedes it could lose all but one
Article:
SUBANG JAYA, Sept 27 — Parti Amanah Negara (Amanah) will identify its general election candidates early to allow them to introduce themselves to voters and to enable the party to make more systematic preparations.
The party’s deputy president, Datuk Seri Dr Mujahid Yusof Rawa, said this move alongside strengthening the party’s machinery and narrative is crucial for Amanah to retain its existing seats and achieve its target of winning more seats in the 16th general election (GE16).
He said Amanah aims to win at least 18 parliamentary seats in GE16, enabling the party to play a greater role in championing the interests of the
ummah
(Muslim community).
“GE16 must be viewed as an uphill battle as party members cannot afford to be complacent. Instead, they must redouble efforts to strengthen grassroots support including increasing the number of branches and members and streamline the machinery at the Polling District Centre level,” he said while addressing the launch of Selangor Amanah election machinery here today.
Mujahid warned that Amanah risks retaining only one parliamentary seat in GE16 if it fails to strengthen its machinery and voter support.
He noted that based on the party’s internal studies and simulations under certain scenarios, only the Kota Raja parliamentary seat held by Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu appears likely to be retained, while other seats would face significant challenges.
Mujahid added that Amanah must also reinforce the Islam
Rahmatan Lil ’Alamin
(Islam as a Mercy to All Creation) narrative as the core of its struggle, including convincing Malay and Muslim voters that the party is capable of protecting and championing their interests without sidelining the rights of non-Muslim and non-Malay communities.
He said voter support can shift when voters feel that their security, economic future, and family interests are better assured under a particular party.
Additionally, Mujahid urged Amanah’s leadership to pay closer attention to grassroots members to prevent them from leaving the party, including by acknowledging their sacrifices and looking after their welfare. — Bernama

Title: MetMalaysia alerts seven states to evening thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 27 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in parts of seven states until 7pm today.
In Perak, the affected area is Hulu Perak, while in Kelantan, the warning covers Kuala Krai, Jeli, Tanah Merah, Machang and Pasir Puteh, MetMalaysia said in a statement.
The warning also covers Besut, Setiu, Dungun, Kemaman, Marang and Hulu Terengganu in Terengganu; Pekan, Rompin and Jerantut in Pahang; and Kota Tinggi and Mersing in Johor.
In Sarawak, the affected areas are Kapit, Betong, Sarikei, Sibu, Mukah, Bintulu, Miri, Limbang, Samarahan, Serian, Kuching and Sri Aman (Lubok Antu).
In Sabah, the warning covers the West Coast (Ranau, Tuaran, Kota Kinabalu, Kota Belud, Penampang and Papar), Interior (Keningau, Tambunan, Pensiangan, Sook, Tenom, Sipitang, Beaufort and Membakut), Kudat (Kota Marudu), and Sandakan (Kinabatangan and Sandakan). — Bernama

Title: Families of 55 missing Malaysians in Nepal want moratorium to ease loans, insurance claims
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 27 — Families of 55 Malaysians still missing following the flash flood in Nepal have urged the government to consider a special moratorium on the victims’ financial commitments, as their families are now facing difficulties accessing the victims’ accounts and assets, insurance coverage, and managing their loans.
Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (MASFIH) spokesperson Dr Manivannan Rethinam said that after 33 days without certainty, financial and legal issues have become among the most pressing concerns for the families, particularly as some of the victims were the main breadwinners.
He explained that the moratorium requested was not for all family members but specifically for financial commitments involving the 55 individuals who remain missing.
“We do not need to wait for the Nepalese government. There are many things we can do in Malaysia now. What we are asking for is a special moratorium for the 55 missing individuals, covering all financial commitments under their names or related to them.
“This will help the families cope until death certificates are issued and insurance claims and estate matters can be settled,” he told reporters after attending a more than four-hour meeting between the next of kin and government agencies at Wisma Putra here today, involving about 105 people.
The session, which began at about 10.15 am and ended around 3 pm, included briefings on search and rescue (SAR) operations, the management of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) samples, as well as legal and documentation processes involving the individuals who remain missing.
Manivannan said the victims’ status as missing persons had placed various constraints on their families, as assets and financial commitments under their names could not be managed as usual.
These included bank accounts, vehicle and housing loans, company interests, and life and travel insurance claims.
He said some families wanted to return their vehicles because they could no longer afford the payments, but faced difficulties because the vehicles were registered in the missing individuals’ names.
As such, MASFIH wants to hold a meeting with Bank Negara Malaysia, the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) and relevant agencies to seek a specific mechanism to resolve the issues faced by the families.
Manivannan said the families have also sought a meeting with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to enable a comprehensive solution to be coordinated at the highest government level.
He said the families appreciated the Prime Minister’s earlier move to contact his counterpart Balendra Shah regarding efforts to establish a special mechanism to address the issue, but believed that several measures could be implemented in Malaysia without having to wait for a decision by the Nepalese government.
On efforts to identify the victims, Manivannan said the families were informed that the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) had obtained 98 DNA samples from next of kin, all of which had been processed by the Department of Chemistry Malaysia as of Sept 24.
He said the process, which normally takes longer, had been expedited to enable matching to be carried out should any bodies be found.
He said three DNA profiles had also been sent to China following information that three of the missing Malaysians had immigration-related records in the Tibet area.
MASFIH, however, urged that the possibility of sending DNA profiles of other members of the same group also be considered if there was evidence that they had been in the area.
According to Manivannan, representatives of the Malaysian Embassy in Beijing had informed them that if families had information indicating that other individuals were also there, the matter could be discussed with the Chinese authorities.
He said the families had also asked PDRM and the Department of Chemistry to reassess whether the DNA samples obtained from each family were sufficient to establish stronger matches.
Manivannan also said the families appreciated the efforts of the relevant teams in explaining the challenges and search operations being conducted in Nepal.
However, the families questioned why the Malaysian team’s operations could not focus on the Rasuwagadhi area near the Nepal-Tibet border, which was believed to be the last known location of some of the missing Malaysians before contact was lost.
According to him, the families were informed that the areas covered by the Malaysian team’s operations were determined based on permission from the Nepalese authorities, while access to certain areas was beyond the control of the SMART team.
He said the families were also informed that there remained a possibility that victims could be found alive if they were in remote areas or villages, although the possibility was considered very slim.
Manivannan said the families were also informed that the Nepalese government was considering ending the SAR phase and moving into the recovery and reconstruction phase, although no date had been set.
At the same time, he said, the Nepalese authorities were working to expedite the DNA matching process, while discussions were also ongoing on documentation mechanisms relating to disaster victims, adding that the families now needed not only information on the search operations but also a clear direction to address the long-term impact. — Bernama

Title: MCMC blocks 101.66 million scam calls with telcos under spoofing gateway from Feb to Aug 2026
Article:
KULAI, Sept 27 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), in collaboration with telecommunications service providers, blocked a total of 101.66 million scam or spoof calls from February to August.
Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said the success was achieved through the implementation of the Inter Operator Spoofing Gateway initiative, which has been in place since the beginning of this year.
She said that scammers from abroad use Caller ID Spoofing tactics to display phone numbers as if they are from local telco networks to deceive victims in this country.
“The total number of spoof calls blocked, amounting to 101.66 million, proves that this initiative is very effective,” she told reporters when met at the Watch a Movie with the Kulai MP programme here today.
She said this when asked to comment on the number of scam calls blocked so far.
Meanwhile, Teo said the MCMC will hold an online meeting with Meta tomorrow regarding public complaints concerning blocked WhatsApp accounts.
She said the meeting was to obtain a detailed briefing regarding the case.
“We (the ministry) will wait for the results (information) from the meeting on that day,” she said.
MCMC had previously reported that it was investigating public complaints regarding WhatsApp accounts that were reported to have been hacked, blocked, or no longer accessible.
The Commission also said that it has submitted the case to Meta for clarification and appropriate action. — Bernama

Title: Evening haze: Unhealthy air quality in five areas nationwide, Johor accounts for four and Sarawak one
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 27 — Five areas, four in Johor and one in Sarawak, recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at an unhealthy level as of 4pm today.
According to data from the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), the areas in Johor recording unhealthy API readings were Pasir Gudang (161), Kota Tinggi (159), Pengerang (158), and Larkin (152).
Meanwhile, in Sarawak, only Serian recorded an unhealthy API reading, at 141.
A total of 51 areas, including Kuala Lumpur, recorded readings at a moderate level, while 12 areas recorded good readings.
API readings between 0 and 50 are categorised as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and 301 and above as hazardous. — Bernama

Title: BN chairman Zahid says coalition will end ties with Pakatan once Parliament dissolves
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 27 — Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today made he saw no possibility of cooperation between his coalition and Pakatan Harapan (PH), amid talks that relations between the two sides have hit “an all time low”.
Speaking at the 18th annual general assembly of the Malaysian Makkal Sakti Party at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur this afternoon, the Umno president “promised” that BN would “part ways” the moment Parliament is dissolved, in an apparent response to calls for the coalition to stop all forms of political cooperation with PH in the Unity Government.
“The moment the current Parliament is dissolved, we will no longer be part of that government,” he said in his opening address today,
The Star
quoted Zahid as saying.
BN and PH are currently in the governing federal coalition, but leaders like Umno’s Khairy Jamaluddin confirmed that ties between Zahid and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim have soured in recent months as the two sides clashed at the Johor and Negeri Sembilan state elections.
At the same event, Parti Makkal Sakti Malaysia president Datuk Seri RS Thanenthiran urged Zahid to pull BN out of the Unity government as soon as possible.
“Parti Makkal Sakti Malaysia proposes that Barisan Nasional leave the Madani Government as soon as possible,” Thanenthiran was quoted as saying by
The Star
.
He also noted that several Umno leaders had faced arrests and investigations, adding that it appeared there were attempts to pressure BN and its leadership into giving way.
The call comes amid talks of internal pressure for BN to end its alliance with PH.
Zahid himself has made comments seen as critical of Anwar at public events, including daring him to call for elections this year, although he has often told reporters on the sidelines that Umno remains “committed” to seeing through its alliance with PH until the end of the term.

Title: Do not compare Penang’s mega projects with one year of Sabah road funding, state PKR tells PAS rival
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 27 — Transport infrastructure development in Sabah remains a priority for the Madani Government, with comparisons between states needing to take into account their respective scale and requirements, said Sabah PKR Information Chief Ahmad Farid Sainuri.
He said Sabah’s roads still required serious attention, including faster completion of the Pan Borneo Highway to narrow the development gap between Sabah and Peninsular Malaysia.
“We do not deny that Sabah’s roads still require serious attention. As Sabahans, we want the Pan Borneo Highway completed faster and the development gap between Sabah and Peninsular Malaysia further narrowed,” he said in a statement today.
Ahmad Farid was responding to the Sabah PAS criticism of the Federal Government’s transport infrastructure priorities following the approval of more than RM21 billion in projects for Penang.
He said the more than RM21 billion cited for Penang comprised mainly large-scale infrastructure projects being implemented over several years, rather than an annual allocation handed to the state government.
“These include the RM16.8 billion Penang LRT project, as well as airport, port and cruise terminal expansion projects,” he said.
Ahmad Farid said Budget 2026 listed the Pan Borneo Highway Sabah Phase 1A and 1B at RM15.9 billion, while the Sarawak-Sabah Link Road Phases 1 and 2 were valued at RM8.81 billion and the Trans Borneo Highway at RM2.99 billion.
“Therefore, it is inaccurate to compare the total value of Penang’s projects solely with one component of Sabah’s road maintenance allocation for a single year. If we include the full value of the Penang LRT, we must also include the full value of the mega projects being implemented in Sabah,” he said.
In the aviation sector, nearly RM500 million has been approved for the expansion of Kota Kinabalu International Airport, while RM120.9 million has been allocated to upgrade Tawau Airport.
According to him, Penang has urban transport, density and congestion problems that require a mass transit system, while Sabah is a much larger region with different geographical challenges.
“Development justice means the Federal Government must develop both based on their respective needs, while giving greater attention to narrowing Sabah’s development gap,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Fire Dept finds nine tiny rooms squeezed into office and turned into student dormitory in Terengganu
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Sept 27 — Small student dormitories built within an office premises were among the conditions detected today by the Terengganu Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) during the Ops Sepadu Premis Sarang Burung operation around Kuala Terengganu.
The premises on the second floor had nine small rooms built separately and converted into student dormitories, in addition to being found non-compliant with several building safety regulations.
Terengganu JBPM director Nor Mahathir Muhammad said that inspections found that the premises in question, along with three other inspected locations, were originally approved as office buildings but had been repurposed for use as dormitories for workers and students.
“In this operation, our focus was on shop premises or office spaces that have been illegally modified, including looking into non-compliance with building regulations and fire safety aspects,” he said when met after the operation here today.
The integrated operation was carried out at four locations, namely Jalan Masjid Abidin, Jalan Engku Pengiran Anom 2, Jalan Engku Sar and Jalan Sultan Zainal Abidin.
“JBPM will issue a notice to the owner or tenant of the premises involved to take action to eliminate the identified fire hazards. If the owner or tenant fails to comply with the notice within the given period, we will conduct a second inspection,” he added. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: JBPM is the Malay abbreviation for Jabatan Bomba dan Penyelamat Malaysia.
